pack.title: Car dealerships
pack.description: Today-only prices and trips to the manager. Decide on your timeline, not theirs.

scenarios.setting: Dealership desk. The salesperson slides the paper across and taps it.
scenarios.jab: This price is only good if you sign today.

replies.line: Then it's not my price. I'll be here Thursday — so will the car.
replies.why: It calls the deadline a bluff by naming a later date with total confidence.
replies.delivery: Stand as you say Thursday. Movement sells it.

replies.why: Two words that end the pressure script because there's nothing to negotiate against.

replies.line: I get the urgency — I still don't decide same-day. What can you do Thursday?
replies.why: It validates his job while holding your rule, then hands him a solvable problem.

replies.line: A price with a bedtime. Interesting. Mine sleeps in.
replies.why: Treating the deadline as absurd makes it absurd, without ever arguing terms.

replies.line: Only good today? Then it's not a price, it's a hostage note.
replies.why: It renames the tactic so bluntly the room has to laugh or drop it.

trap.line: Fine — but you're ripping me off and we both know it.
trap.why: Signing while accusing him gets you the worst price and the worst story.

scenarios.setting: Finance office. The manager leans back after your counteroffer.
scenarios.jab: You know what? Let me go talk to my manager. Stay right there.

replies.line: Take your time. My number doesn't move while you walk.
replies.why: It names your price as fixed before the theater starts, so the theater has no audience.
It grants the trip while freezing the terms, which is the whole game.

replies.line: Of course — tell him I'm an easy yes at my number.
replies.why: It makes you the reasonable one and gives the manager a face-saving path to yes.

replies.line: Bring him back. I love a live negotiation show.
replies.why: Naming the ritual as entertainment deflates it for everyone in earshot.

replies.line: Tell him the car can wait. So can I.
replies.why: It removes every deadline from the room, which is the only leverage he brought.

trap.line: Whatever — just tell me the lowest you'll actually go.
trap.why: Asking for the floor first hands him your ceiling to negotiate down from.

scenarios.setting: After the test drive. The salesperson walks you past the car you asked about.
scenarios.jab: For just a little more a month, you could be in this one instead.

replies.line: I'm here for the one I asked about. Let's price that.
replies.why: It redirects to your target without debating the upgrade, which starves the upsell.
It refuses the redirect in four words and points back at your car.

replies.line: She's beautiful — and she's someone else's. Mine's the one we drove.
replies.why: Admiring the car while declining it keeps him working for you, not the commission.

replies.line: A little more a month is still more. Price the car I drove.
replies.why: It translates monthly-speak back into real money, which ends the framing trick.

replies.line: My budget and I are exclusive.
replies.why: Treating the budget as a relationship makes the upsell the other party.
